keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Mainland Australia without Tasmania (31,226 land cells, about 7.9 M km2). The page says people arrived 50,000-65,000 years ago ("Madjedbebe ... as early as 65,000 years BP") and is "silent on whether people occupied the whole continent, including the arid interior"; the Prehistory page gives no occupation map for 6000-3400 BCE, so the whole mainland is drawn at low confidence. No infobox area exists.

ledger.note: 6000 BCE (project floor): Aboriginal Australian cultures hold the mainland. The people have lived on the continent since "as early as 65,000 years BP" (Madjedbebe), long before the floor; "Aboriginal Australians" are "the various peoples indigenous to mainland Australia and associated islands, excluding the Torres Strait Islands". The page does not say the arid interior was occupied in this era, so the extent is the dossier's bridging judgment; Tasmania is cut off by the Bass Strait flooding "around 6000 BCE" (Aboriginal Tasmanians page).

ledger.note: 3400 BCE (end of the cultures horizon): the dossier stops here but the Aboriginal cultures continue. The dossier stops at -3400, the horizon of the cultures group (Cliopatria holds nothing before 3400 BCE and no later group draws this land until the colonies); the culture itself does not end there. The Indigenous Australians page gives pre-1788 population estimates of 318,000 to more than 3,000,000 and does not date the end of the pre-colonial era for the whole continent.

certainty.note: No border is recorded; about 600 nations or tribes are named on the page without a map.

sources.title: Indigenous Australians
sources.note: People arrived 50,000-65,000 years ago; "mainland Australia and associated islands, excluding the Torres Strait Islands"; 600 tribes or nations, 250 languages; pre-1788 population estimates.

sources.title: Prehistory of Australia
sources.note: Sea levels stabilised about 6,500 years ago; islands formed 8,000-6,000 years ago; the Australian Small Tool tradition 5,000-3,000 years ago.

sources.title: Torres Strait Islanders
sources.note: Opened and not used for any event: gives no dates for the formation or settlement of the Torres Strait islands; "The core of Island culture is Papuan"; "Ethnically distinct from the Aboriginal peoples of the rest of Australia".

notes: Aboriginal Australians, mainland. The two pages give no dated extent for 6000-3400 BCE, so the whole mainland (Tasmania and the Torres Strait Islands excepted by the page) is a confidence-1 placement. Dated facts in the window, none a border change: sea levels "stabilised at around their current level about 6,500 years ago" (4550 BCE) and "between 8,000 and 6,000 years ago thousands of islands in the Torres Strait and around the coast of Australia were formed" (Prehistory page); the Australian Small Tool tradition "between 5,000 years ago and 3,000 years ago" (that is 3050-1050 BCE, after the horizon). The dossier ends at -3400 by the group's convention; the culture runs to the colonies (the Indigenous Australians page: "Before 1788, estimates range from 318,000"), which no dossier of this batch draws: the orchestrator should extend this dossier (or have the colonial group take the land from it) so that Australia is not blank from 3399 BCE to the colonies. Torres Strait Islanders ("The first phase of occupation of the Torres Strait Islands began about 4,000 years ago", Indigenous Australians page) start after the horizon and have no dossier. The islands of the Torres Strait are inside the Australia country cells drawn here (a few cells).
